messages:
incident-bot: Pager: P1 - edenbridge production auth errors (VPC). Affected: edenbridge-prod (dedicated pool). Symptoms: 401 from tenant auth, spikes in failed assertions. Trigger: high 401 rate from tenant bridge.

ryan-oncall: I'm on it. Paging in to SRE rotation. @lia can you confirm customer impact?

lia-customer-success: Customer says alerts started ~10m ago, API calls failing for their web traffic. They report 30% of requests failing with 401s, mostly new sessions.

ingrid-ps: Observed increased 401 in logs: `authbridge/tenant: token validation failed: kid not found` for many requests. Looks like their OIDC provider rotated keys.

maya-infra: Confirmed. Our JWKS fetches show edenbridge OIDC JWKS returning a new key set but `kid` that some tokens reference isn't present in new set. Could be token replay of older token signed by old key that was removed prematurely.

ellis-security: If the customer rotated keys but didn't publish overlap period or didn't keep old key for TTL, tokens in flight will fail. Need to check our JWKS cache TTL and fallback behavior.

ryan-oncall: Immediate mitigations? Can we fall back to last-known-good JWKS or enable a temporary permissive validation?

maya-infra: We have two levers: 1) force a JWKS refresh for edenbridge bridge and accept cached previous set for 5m longer; 2) flip tenant-auth fallback to use signed-token acceptance window (dangerous). Prefer 1.

ingrid-ps: Also, edenbridge uses private VPC deployment with auth-proxy in front; their IDP (cust-oidc) might be behind a propagation delay. Lia - are they able to re-issue tokens on their side?

lia-customer-success: They said rotation was manual and they can re-issue tokens, but their engineers are coordinating with their identity team. Asking them to re-issue short-lived tokens now.

ryan-oncall: Let's do these steps in parallel:
- maya: JWKS refresh + extend cached previous JWKS acceptance for tenant `edenbridge-prod` (no global change).
- ingrid: add temporary request logging sample for failed token with headers for investigation.
- ellis: verify audit/decision if we need to relax validation rules (last resort).
- lia: keep customer updated and ask them to rotate back or re-issue tokens.

maya-infra: Running JWKS refresh now against edenbridge OIDC endpoint: `curl -s https://oidc.edenbridge.local/.well-known/jwks.json | jq .`
maya-infra: Found two key sets: previous (kid: `K-2023-AB`) and current (`K-2026-XY`). The token kid being presented in logs is `K-2023-AB` which is absent in the current live set. However we still have previous in our cache (stale). I can extend acceptance for that cached set for 15m.

ryan-oncall: Do it. Add a scoped config so only edenbridge-prod acceptance window changed. Document change id: `cfg-incident-3309876543`

maya-infra: Done: `PATCH /internal/tenants/edenbridge-prod/config` -> \"jwks.accept_stale_seconds\": 900 (applied to bridge). Rollout id `rollout-7f3a`.

deploy-bot: Rollout `rollout-7f3a` started on 6 nodes, progress: 2/6 updated.

ingrid-ps: Capturing a failed token sample for the SRE investigation:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IkstMjAyMy1BQiJ9... (kid: K-2023-AB)
x-forwarded-for: 10.12.45.3
```

ellis-security: I'm watching logs and audit trails. Quick check: no signs of token replay attack; appears legitimate. Approving temporary acceptance of cached JWKS.

lia-customer-success: Customer confirmed they're issuing new tokens now. They plan to backfill tokens later. Asking about how long until service normal.

ryan-oncall: Monitoring. After rollout finishes we'll see if 401s drop. If they persist, we may need to enable a permissive validation mode that accepts tokens signed by the previously rotated key for a longer window — but that requires higher-level approval.

deploy-bot: Rollout `rollout-7f3a` completed: 6/6 updated.

maya-infra: Metrics: 401 error rate for edenbridge-prod dropped from 30% -> 4% over the last 6 minutes. Latency normal.

lia-customer-success: Customer reports traffic mostly recovered. They still see some failed sessions in older browser clients. They're okay with recovery and will coordinate to re-issue tokens for those clients.

ingrid-ps: Collecting root-cause artifacts: JWKS rotation without overlap, tokens with old kid, our default JWKS ttl was 60s with aggressive caching. We'll recommend config changes.

ellis-security: Action: file post-incident ticket for policy: require overlap window on customer rotations or recommend minimum `rotate-withoverlap` guidance. Also need internal change to support longer default stale acceptance for dedicated pools for customers who request it.

ryan-oncall: Agreed. Next steps during incident and postmortem:
- Immediate: monitor 1h and keep acceptance window for 15m more (config `cfg-incident-3309876543` extended to 1800s)
- Short term (24h): coordinate with edenbridge to publish an overlap window and confirm full redeploy of their sessions
- Postmortem: RFC for JWKS handling in tenant bridge (backwards compatibility, caching semantics, feature flag to allow per-tenant stale-JWKS settings).

maya-infra: Extended `jwks.accept_stale_seconds` to 1800 for edenbridge-prod. Change id `cfg-incident-3309876543-extend`.

lia-customer-success: Edenbridge thanks the team. Their SRE asks for an audit log of token failures for compliance. 

ingrid-ps: Uploaded sampled failed tokens/logs to secure bucket `s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/3309876543/` and shared a signed link with edenbridge SRE.

ellis-security: Filing INC-3309876543 on internal tracker with severity=P1 -> will include timeline, artifacts, decision rationale for temporary acceptance window.

ryan-oncall: Handoff to oncall-night (ellis) at 22:00 UTC. If errors spike above 10% again, escalate to eng-infra and page product-owner.

ellis-security: Taking over. I'll monitor and keep lia in loop. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident P1 status updated -> \"Mitigated (customer-impact reduced)\". Next update scheduled in 30m.

ryan-oncall: Closing handoff notes: commands run, configs changed, rollouts, artifact links in ticket.

lia-customer-success: Client follow-up scheduled for 10:00 their local time tomorrow.

ellis-security: last check: 401 rate stable ~2-3%. No further action unless customer requests.

ryan-oncall: Thanks team.
